subject: Food Science
title: Sound Affects Taste
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sound Affects Taste.

hook.text: Play high-pitched music and chocolate tastes sweeter. Play low-pitched and the same chocolate tastes more bitter.

buildup.text: Charles Spence at Oxford proved that auditory cues modulate taste perception through cross-modal sensory interaction in the brain.

discovery.text: Airline food tastes bland partly because engine noise (85 dB) suppresses sweet and salty perception by up to 30%.

twist.text: Crunchiness is partly auditory. When researchers reduced the crunch sound of chips through headphones, subjects rated them as.

climax.text: Some restaurants now design 'sonic seasoning'—pairing menu items with specific background music to enhance particular flavors.

punchline.text: Your ears flavor your food. High notes sweeten. Loud noise dulls. Silence changes nothing.

quiz.question: Why does airplane food taste bland?
